title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
technique: one-shot weight-only post-training quantization (3-4 bit) via approximate second-order (OBQ-style) updates; dequantizing matrix-vector kernels

optimized_metrics.evidence: the parameters of GPT3-175B occupy 326GB (counting in multiples of 1024) of memory when stored in a compact float16 format. This exceeds the capacity of even the highest-end single GPUs, and thus inference must be performed using more complex and expensive setups, such as multi-GPU deployments.
precise enough to compress such models to 3 or 4 bits per parameter without significant loss of accuracy
language generation, one of the most appealing applications of these models, with the goal of latency reduction
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: Table 6: Average per-token latency (batch size 1) when generating sequences of length 128.

optimized_metrics.evidence: efficient enough to execute on models with hundreds of billions of parameters in at most a few hours

headline_claim.text: end-to-end inference speedups over FP16, of around 3.25x when using high-end GPUs (NVIDIA A100) and 4.5x when using more cost-effective ones (NVIDIA A6000)

reported_metrics.where: Tables 1-5, Fig 1-3 (perplexity on WikiText2/PTB/C4, zero-shot accuracy)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Table 6: Average per-token latency (batch size 1) when generating sequences of length 128.
metric_definitions.notes: Single-sequence decoding; FP16 baseline run on multiple GPUs (5x A100 or 8x A6000), quantized model on 1 A100 / 2 A6000, so speedup mixes quantization and GPU-count reduction (communication costs described as negligible).

tradeoff_acknowledged: Method gives no speedup for the actual multiplications (no hardware support for mixed-precision operands); speedups come from reduced memory movement; 3-bit has noticeably higher perplexity for smaller models
workloads: WikiText2, PTB, C4 perplexity; LAMBADA, ARC, PIQA zero-shot
extractor_notes: Primarily accuracy-vs-bitwidth/memory; latency is a secondary measured benefit at batch 1. The 3.25x/4.5x headline compares 1 A100 (3-bit) with 5 A100 FP16 (and 2xA6000 vs 8xA6000), i.e. GPU-count reduction included.
load_class_quote: Average per-token latency (batch size 1) when generating sequences of length 128. (Table 6)
